$comment: Machine-readable record of the official-source verification performed for the Open 3D Model (Open3Dmodel) project. Every field here was read from the official pages listed in `pages_verified`, on the date in `accessed`. Nothing in this file is inferred, assumed, or filled in from memory.

project.name: Open 3D Anatomical Model for Education ('Open3Dmodel')
platform_operators: Department of Anatomy & Embryology, Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC), Netherlands
Faculty of Health, Medicine & Life Science, Maastricht University (UM), Netherlands
project.platform_support: Dutch Association of Anatomists (Nederlandse Anatomen Vereniging, NAV)
project.funding: Grant from the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (surf.nl), obtained 2022

pages_verified.purpose: project overview, stated licence intent, roadmap
licence chain, provenance, anatomy-review method, status
source files and selection models — actual download links

how_it_was_stated.about_page: "further develop an open-licensed (Creative Commons Attribute ShareAlike CC BY SA) 3D model of human anatomy" with a direct link to the CC BY-SA 4.0 deed
how_it_was_stated.derivative_clause: "The creation and distribution of any derivative materials from the open3dmodel should comply with the Creative Commons license's requirements stated with the material."
how_it_was_stated.license_version_confirmed_by: The linked deed URL path ends in /4.0/

ambiguities_found.finding: The landing page states the licence in the FUTURE tense: "The model WILL BE licensed under Creative Commons Attribution ShareAlike (CC BY SA)".
ambiguities_found.detail: The About page is more affirmative about the grant's intent and links the BY-SA 4.0 deed, but the landing page — the page a downloader most often lands on — describes the licence as a goal rather than a current fact.
ambiguities_found.why_it_matters: Whether a licence is currently in force, or intended, determines whether redistribution obligations apply today or later. This cannot be resolved from the published pages alone.

ambiguities_found.finding: The distributed archives contain NO licence file, NO README and NO attribution notice.
ambiguities_found.detail: Verified by downloading upper-limb-glb.zip (SHA-256 5AF0190A6D7BF47393447AC30021E4F3BA619721C7F3A620C39A895947078432): the archive contains exactly one entry, `upper-limb.glb`. Nothing else.
ambiguities_found.why_it_matters: The About page requires derivative materials to comply with "the Creative Commons license's requirements stated with the material". No such statement ships with the material, so the operative terms attached to the file itself cannot be confirmed from the file.

ambiguities_found.finding: The AnatomyTOOL landing page self-describes as "Non-commercial, University based."
ambiguities_found.detail: This describes the PLATFORM, not the model. CC BY-SA 4.0 itself permits commercial reuse. Whether any separate, model-specific non-commercial restriction exists could not be found on the official pages.
ambiguities_found.why_it_matters: CC BY-SA 4.0 permits commercial use, so this is probably not a restriction on the model. It must nonetheless be confirmed before any commercial release, because the page is ambiguous about what it scopes.

ambiguities_found.finding: Three generations of CC BY-SA are stacked in the provenance chain.
ambiguities_found.detail: BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA) -> Z-Anatomy (CC BY-SA) -> Open3Dmodel (CC BY-SA). The viewer code is separately GPL3.
ambiguities_found.why_it_matters: ShareAlike is transitive. Any Adapted Material carries CC BY-SA 4.0 obligations regardless of which generation it was derived from. This is manageable, but the attribution chain must be preserved in full, not truncated to the most recent generation.

share_alike_obligations.applies_to: the adapted model file, not the surrounding application
share_alike_obligations.basis: CC BY-SA 4.0 section 3(b)(1); Creative Commons' own FAQ states the ShareAlike condition applies to the Adapted Material and not to the larger work into which it is incorporated
share_alike_obligations.practical_consequence: The application source may remain under a separate, more restrictive licence PROVIDED the model derivative is distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0, is clearly separated, and is accompanied by the required attribution and licence copy.

incompatibility_with_current_project_lic.verdict: Compatible ONLY IF the model derivative is kept under CC BY-SA 4.0 and separated from proprietary code. If the project owner intends the shipped model file to be proprietary, or to be distributed under terms more restrictive than CC BY-SA 4.0, that intent is NOT compatible and the integration must not ship.
incompatibility_with_current_project_lic.decision_owner: project owner / legal counsel — this is a business decision, not an engineering one

required_attribution.basis: CC BY-SA 4.0 section 3(a)(1) and 3(a)(3), plus the project's own instruction that credits are published with the material
must_record: Notice that a licence was applied to the work
Indication that modifications were made, including a description of them
Retention of notices about how the material was modified

contributor_roster.note: The project publishes a named roster with degrees and institutional affiliations. CC BY-SA attribution requires reasonable identification of the author(s). For a model of this provenance, the reasonable reading is that the roster must be reproduced, not summarised.

provenance_chain.name: Voxel models (MRI-derived)
provenance_chain.origin: Japanese groups: National Institute of Informatics, Kitasato University, Keio University, Tokyo Metropolitan University
provenance_chain.licence: not stated on the Open3Dmodel pages for this generation
provenance_chain.note: 3D human voxel models for electromagnetic dosimetry, based on MRI of a 22-year-old male and female volunteer

provenance_chain.name: BodyParts3D
provenance_chain.origin: Database Center for Life Science, Japan
provenance_chain.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA); the About page links the BY-SA 4.0 deed
provenance_chain.reference: Mitsuhashi N et al. 2008/2009, NAR vol 37, PMID 18835852
provenance_chain.note: Segmented into separate 3D models of 382 body parts

provenance_chain.name: Z-Anatomy
provenance_chain.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA); the About page links the BY-SA 4.0 deed
modifications_from_predecessor: meshes simplified / retopologized to reduce file size
vessels and nerves converted into curves

provenance_chain.name: Open3Dmodel
provenance_chain.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0) — see ambiguities above
modifications_from_predecessor: all structures remeshed / retopologized to remove 'hooked' surface artefacts
each structure reviewed for anatomical correctness by one to three anatomists
muscles, tendons and aponeuroses added or adapted
joint capsules, articular cartilages, bursae, synovial sheaths modelled
all blood vessels and nerves of the upper and lower limb newly modelled

anatomical_review_method.reviewers_per_structure: 1 to 3 anatomists with expertise in the specific topic
anatomical_review_method.stated_caveat: "Despite our best efforts, some errors may still be present."

adjacent_but_separate_licence.name: open3dviewer
adjacent_but_separate_licence.applies_to: the viewer software only, not the model
adjacent_but_separate_licence.note: GPL3 on the viewer is a CODE licence. It does not apply to the anatomical model. Do not copy viewer source into Muscle Atlas without a GPL3 assessment — Muscle Atlas is not GPL3.

available_downloads.directory_listing: HTTP 403 — directory browsing disabled; files are reachable by direct link only

no_pack_available_for.finding: There is NO downloadable thorax / abdomen / back muscle pack at the time of verification.
no_pack_available_for.detail: The project landing page lists "Muscles of thorax, abdomen and back (March 2026)" as a workstream item, not as a released, downloadable pack. The create page offers only upper-limb, lower-limb and hand among muscle-relevant packs.
no_pack_available_for.consequence: Muscle Atlas structures whose 3D counterpart would live in a thorax/abdomen/back pack cannot currently be sourced from an official download.

inspected_artifacts.naming_convention_observed: Terminologia Anatomica names, right side suffixed `.r` (e.g. "Long head of biceps brachii.r"), grouped into collections such as "Arm - muscles", "Arm - bones"

inspected_artifacts.note: Header-level inspection only; not extracted or retained. Inspecting was sufficient to confirm structure, naming and budget, and was deliberately done in a temporary directory.

muscle_atlas_coverage_check.method: Node-name substring search across the union of upper-limb and lower-limb node names
muscle_atlas_coverage_check.coverage: 14 of 19 structures have a candidate 3D counterpart; 5 do not.
muscle_atlas_coverage_check.false_positive_warning: A naive substring search produces false positives. 'Oblique' matched only unrelated nodes (radio-ulnar syndesmosis, oblique ligament of the 1st finger, oblique head of adductor pollicis). 'Serratus' matched bursae as well as the muscle. Every mapping must be confirmed by a human against the actual node list, never by substring match alone.

blocking_questions.question: Is CC BY-SA 4.0 currently in force for the model, or is it the stated intent for a future release?
blocking_questions.why_blocking: The landing page uses future tense ("will be licensed"); the About page links the BY-SA 4.0 deed as though current.
blocking_questions.who_can_answer: the Open3Dmodel project, via https://anatomytool.org/open3dmodel-contact or the NAV (Nederlandse Anatomen Vereniging)

blocking_questions.question: What is the exact licence instrument that ships with the downloadable GLB/OBJ/Blend files, given that the archives contain no licence file?
blocking_questions.why_blocking: CC BY-SA requires the licence to accompany the material. As shipped, it does not.

blocking_questions.question: Is the project owner willing and able to distribute the model derivative under CC BY-SA 4.0 while keeping the application source under a more restrictive licence?
blocking_questions.why_blocking: If the answer is no, the integration must not ship in any form.
blocking_questions.workaround: none — but see proposed_alternatives in the integration doc

integration_decision.reason: Instruction: "Do not integrate any file before the source/license record is complete." Q1 and Q2 are unresolved, so the record is not complete. Committing a derived model under an unverified licence is the exact failure mode the integration brief was written to prevent.
integration_decision.what_was_built_instead: The complete 3D integration architecture, mapping data derived from verified node names, validators, capability detection, offline model management, attribution presentation, and the full documentation set — with the model packs deliberately absent and every runtime path degrading honestly to the 2D board.
